questions.question: India was divided into India and Pakistan by the ______ Act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India Independence**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__** 

__
 
• India was divided into India and Pakistan by the **India Independence Act, 1947.**
 
• India Independence Act, 1947 was an Act of the British Parliament that partitioned India into two dominions of **India and Pakistan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Act put **Mountbatten Plan** into force, which was the last plan for independence.
 
• **The Mountbatten Plan or the 3 June Plan-**
 
 
• The June 3 plan, also known as the Mountbatten Plan included these principles:-
 
 

 
• The principle of the partition of British India was accepted by the British Government
 
• Successor governments would be given dominion status
 
• Autonomy and sovereignty to both countries
 
• Can make their own constitution.

 
• **Features of India Independence Act, 1947-**

 
 
• **Division of British India into the two new dominions of India and Pakistan**, with effect from August 15, 1947.
 
• **Partition of the provinces of Bengal and Punjab** between the two new countries.
 
• Establishment of the** office of Governor-General** in each of the two new countries, as representatives of the Crown.
 
• Conferral of **complete legislative authority upon the respective Constituent Assemblies** of the two new countries.
 
• **Termination of British suzerainty over the princely states**, with effect from 15 August 1947, and recognised the **right of states to remain independent or accede to either dominion.**
 
• **Abolition of the use of the title "Emperor of India"** by the British monarch.
 
• The Act also made provision for the **division of joint property,** etc. between the two new countries, including in particular the division of the armed forces.

questions.question: The Purna Kumbh Mela takes place every ________ years at one of the four places by rotation, Prayag, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **Purna Kumbh Mela **takes place every **twelve years** at one of the four places by rotation, **Prayag, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.**
 
• **Kumbh Mela -**__ 
 
 
• The Kumbh Mela is a major Hindu festival and pilgrimage.
 
• The mela is held every three years, and switches between four different locations – **Haridwar (river Ganga**), **Prayag (Triveni sangam of Yamuna, Ganga and Saraswati)**, **Ujjain (river Kshipra)**, and **Nasik (river Godavari)**
 
• The mela returns to each location after a span of **12 years**.
 
• The Kumbh Mela is related to the Hindu mythological story of ***“Samudra Manthan”*** or the churning of nectar.
 
• The **“kumbh”** actually means ***pot***, signifying the pot holding the Amrita (nectar) churned out during Samudra Manthan.
 
• As per the story, after Samudra Manthan, the Asuras ran behind devas to get the nectar of immortality.
 
• During the chase some of the nectar fell on the four locations and hence these four locations are worshiped and revered.
 
• Hindus believe bathing in the holy water at the four locations during Kumbh washes away their sins and bless them with divine power.

• The most important function of the lungs is to **take oxygen from the environment and transfer it to the bloodstream.**

__
 
• **Wild Yak**, scientifically known as **Bos mutus**, is a large, long-haired bovine species native to the **Himalayan region, Tibetan Plateau, and parts of Central Asia**.
 
• It is classified as a **wild species** and is distinct from domesticated yaks (**Bos grunniens**).
 
• Wild yaks are primarily found at **high altitudes of around 3,000 to 5,500 meters**, where they thrive in cold, arid regions.
 
• They are known for their **thick, long fur** that provides insulation against freezing temperatures.
 
• The wild yak is a **herbivorous animal**, feeding mainly on grasses, mosses, and lichens found in its habitat.
 
• They play a vital role in the ecosystem as they help in the **dispersal of seeds** and nutrient cycling within their environment.
 
• The **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** categorizes the wild yak as **Vulnerable** due to habitat loss, hunting, and hybridization with domestic yaks.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve their population through wildlife protection laws and habitat restoration programs.

• Horses have been domesticated for thousands of years and are used for **transportation, agriculture, and sports**.
 
• They are known for their **speed, endurance, and intelligence**.

• They are commonly used for **plowing fields**, pulling carts, and other agricultural activities.

• Water buffaloes are widely used in **agriculture and milk production**.

questions.solution:
__
 
• Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is the **world's richest cricket board** as of year 2018.

 
• **BCCI -**__

 __
 
• It is the national governing body for cricket in India.
 
• The board was formed in **December 1928****.**
 
• It is headquartered at** Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.**
 
• **Grant Govan** was its **first president.**
 
• **Anthony De Mello** was its **first secretary****.**

 __

Sourav Ganguly

 
 
 

 
 
**CEO**

 
 
 
Rahul Johri

 
 
 

 
 
**Secretary**

 
 
 
Jay Shah

 
 
 

 
 
**Men’s Coach**

 
 
 
Ravi Shastri

 
 
 

 
 
**Women’s Coach**

 
 
 
W V Raman

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Lodha Committee – __**
 
• The supreme Court of India appointed Lodha committee in 2015 for –
 __
 
• Analysing and recommending implementable actions for improving the BCCI.
 
• Assess the quantum of punishment for Gurunath Meiyappan and Raj Kundra in the Indian Premier League (IPL) betting scandal.
 
 
 
• **Reforms suggested by Lodha Committee – __**
 
 
• **The retirement age to be fixed at 70 years**.
 
• Any administrator who (a) has criminal charge/s, (b) is of unsound mind, (c) is insolvent, and (d) holds a position in any other athletic association needs to be removed.
 
• The tenure of any officer bearer to be fixed for **two consecutive terms.**
 
• **A "one vote per state" policy** to make BCCI more transparent in its dealings.
 
• BCCI President cannot have a **tenure of more than two years**.
 
• An independent and sovereign governing body for the IPL.
 
• To ensure that BCCI officials are not involved in any betting,** they need to disclose their assets to the governing board.**
